items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Terminology 30:1
items.html: See “wall.” For the externality and the internality in the wall of the vessel are considered two halves of the wall of the vessel. That is, the half of the “thickness of the wall” that is the coarser is called the internality of the vessel, and it serves the inner light; and the half of the coarseness in the wall that is not so coarse is called the externality of the vessel, and it serves the surrounding light. (Part 4, Chapter 5, Item 3)
